title: Quantum Observatory news item
description: A dated event, not a readiness claim. News and frontier items are kept in separate collections deliberately: the board maps how close things are to real, and a stream of announcements mixed into it would corrupt that map. News points AT the board through `about`, and at the research behind it through `establishedBy`.

headline.description: What happened, in the board's own words. Never a copied headline.

pillar.description: The board covers one domain. The field is kept so a second could be added without a migration, and so every record still says which it is.

date.description: When it happened, not when it was found.

plain.description: What this means for a reader who is not a specialist, and why it matters. The field most people will read.

significance.description: headline = would change what someone plans around · notable = worth knowing · routine = the record. Only headline items are prominent.

corroboration.description: Independent reports of the same event. A single vendor press release with no corroboration is not a story.

validation.description: Why this is believed. An unvalidated item is not published.

checks.description: What was actually done: which primary source was opened, what independent report was found, what was ruled out.

about.description: Frontier item ids this bears on. How news attaches to the map.

establishedBy.description: The research this rests on. The link that makes an announcement traceable to the work behind it.

measurements.description: Figures this event reported, structured so they can be plotted. A news item is dated by WHEN THE THING HAPPENED, which makes it the only place on the board that can carry a capability series — a frontier item holds the current best value and overwrites its own history. Only record a figure the item's own sources state; this is transcription, not inference.

kind.description: What was measured. A closed list on purpose: an open one becomes a second, informal metric name field and nothing can be compared.

qualifier.description: The distinction that stops two numbers being confused — 'error-corrected' against 'error-detected' on the same device, or 'physical' against 'algorithmic'. Without it 48 and 94 look like the same measurement.

modality.description: Which physical platform. Required for anything plotted over time: qubit counts on different platforms are not points on one curve, and a trend drawn across them would be the apples-to-oranges the board's own precedent forbids.

crossChecks.description: Frontier item id whose verified metrics carry this same figure, where one does. A measurement that agrees with something the board already checked is stronger than one that stands alone.
